title: WPSS/4317/2018 of LAXMAN JI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 4317 of 2018
Laxman Ji .....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Another ...Respondents
Present : Mr. K.K. Harbola, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Tej Singh Bisht, Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand
Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate for respondent No. 2
Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 The petitioner has retired from the services of the department of
respondent No. 2 as "Head Assistant" on 30.06.2017. The petitioner in para 7 of
the present writ petition has prayed for the payment of retiral dues which
includes the payment of arrears of 7th Pay Commission, which is extracted
hereunder:-
A. Leave Encashment (300 days) = Rs. 5,91,760/- (approx.)
(sanctioned but not paid)
B. Gratuity = Rs. 9,76,404/- (approx.)
(sanctioned but not paid)
C. Arrear of salary = Rs. 44,095/-(approx.)
 (sanctioned but not paid)
D. Arrears of Pension w.e.f. October 2017
to January, 2018 = Rs. 17,109/- (approx.)
 (sanctioned but not paid)
E. Remaining Dues w.e.f 01.01.2017
to 30.06.2017 = Rs. 58,121/- (approx.)
 (sanctioned but not paid
F. Arrear of 7th Pay Commission = Rs. 13,473/- (approx.)
 w.e.f. 01.01.2017 to 30.09.2017
Rs. 10,94,844/- (approx.)
 Total amount = Rs. 17,00,962/-
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner
has moved several representations but despite of the fact that the
respondent authority, vide their letter No. 64/C.R. No. 513 dated
28.02.2018 had sanctioned the benefit of gratuity Rs. 9,76,404/- and other
benefits i.e. leave encashment i.e. Rs. 5,91,760/- along with other dues
(Annexure No. 1colly to the writ petition), still despite of sanction, the
same has not been remitted the petitioner.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the issue is
squarely covered by the judgement dated 11.09.2018 passed by this Court
in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 3165 of 2018, judgement of Division Bench of
this Court dated 30.11.2015 rendered in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 494 of

2
2015, Writ Petition (S/B) No. 73 of 2918 dated 14.02.2018, Writ Petition
(S/S) No. 113 of 2018, Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1576 of 2018 dated
14.06.2018 and also the judgement passed by the learned Single Judge
dated 25.07.2018 rendered in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2402 of 2018. This
fact, that the controversy is covered by the aforesaid judgements is not
disputed by the learned counsel for the respondent. Hence, this writ petition
is disposed of with a writ of mandamus directing respondent No. 2 to pay
the petitioner post retiral dues as explained in para 7 of the writ petition as
under:
A. Leave Encashment (300 days) = Rs. 5,91,760/- (approx.)
(sanctioned but not paid)
(Within three months)
B. Gratuity = Rs. 9,76,404/- (approx.)
(sanctioned but not paid)
(Within two months)
C. Arrear of salary = Rs. 44,095/-(approx.)
 (sanctioned but not paid)
(Within two months)
D. Arrears of Pension w.e.f. October 2017
to January, 2018 = Rs. 17,109/- (approx.)
 (sanctioned but not paid)
(Within two months)
E. Remaining Dues w.e.f 01.01.2017
to 30.06.2017 = Rs. 58,121/- (approx.)
 (sanctioned but not paid
(Within two months)
4. As far as relief prayed for the payment of arrear of 7th Pay
Commission is concerned, that would be remitted in accordance with the
judgement as rendered by the Division Bench in Writ Petition No. 530
(SB) of 2018, Munna Lal Gupta Vs. State of Uttarakhand and others as
decided on 20th November, 2018.
5. Subject to the above observations, the writ petition stands
disposed of.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 20.12.2018
Mahinder/
